title: QA Dashboard Report
description: Validates a single QA report JSON file for the QA Dashboard application. The report must have a meta block, a test_cases array, and a bugs array.

_comment.description: Optional human-readable comment. Delete before uploading — it is ignored by the validator.

meta.description: Metadata describing the test run: who ran it, on what product, on what date.

report_id.description: Optional unique label for this report. Auto-generated from the filename if omitted.

product.description: Product folder name. Must be fully lowercase and match the first subfolder under qa-data/ exactly.

platform.description: Platform folder name. Must be fully lowercase and match the second subfolder under qa-data/{product}/.

module.description: Module folder name. Must be fully lowercase and match the third subfolder and the report filename prefix.

date.description: Date the tests were run, in YYYYMMDD format (no dashes or slashes).

tester.description: Optional. Name of the person who executed the tests.

test_cases.description: All test cases executed in this run. May be an empty array [] if no tests were run.

items.description: A single test case with its outcome.

tc_id.description: Unique test case identifier within this file. Must not be duplicated.

scenario.description: Optional. Broad feature area or user journey this test belongs to.

title.description: Short human-readable description of what this test verifies.

precondition.description: Optional. Required application state before the tester begins the steps.
examples: A user account exists with email tester@example.com

steps.description: Ordered list of actions the tester performs to execute this test.

expected.description: What the application should do if it is working correctly.
examples: User is redirected to the dashboard

actual.description: What the application actually did when the tester ran this test.
examples: User was redirected to the dashboard

priority.description: Urgency level. P1 = critical (fix before release), P4 = low (cosmetic).

status.description: Outcome of running this test case.

notes.description: Optional. Free-text observations from the tester — flakiness, environment quirks, etc.
examples: Reproducible 100% of the time on Chrome 124

bugs.description: All bugs discovered during this test run. May be an empty array [] if no bugs were found.

bug_id.description: Unique bug identifier within this file.

tc_id.description: The tc_id of the test case that discovered this bug. Should match an existing tc_id in this file — if not, the bug is marked as an orphan on the dashboard.

examples: Login returns HTTP 500 on invalid password

description.description: Optional. Longer explanation of what the bug is and when it occurs.
examples: When user enters wrong password, the server throws an unhandled exception...

steps.description: Step-by-step instructions to reproduce the bug.

expected.description: What the application should have done (the correct behaviour).
examples: HTTP 401 with a user-friendly error message

actual.description: What the application actually did (the broken behaviour).
examples: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error with a Java stack trace

severity.description: Business impact of the bug. CRITICAL = app unusable or security risk, LOW = cosmetic.

status.description: Current lifecycle state of the bug.

notes.description: Optional. Workarounds, PR links, environment details, or any extra context.
examples: Fix in review on PR #88. Regression since v2.4.1.
